title: White gangs on the way to the stores
summary: Segregation in Jackson: gangs of white boys ambushed Black children going to the chain stores across Capitol Street.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Tell me more about what it was like in Jackson(?) racially?

Well, it wasn't exactly all peaches and cream, you know. We still had to deal with the segregation situation, even though we had some things that really were to the opposite fences... Like, in most neighborhoods, there were Black people and White people living next door to each other, especially near the borderline, you know. And no problems until you got to a certain age. When you started going into your teens, that's when the dividing line came, you know. And different neighborhoods... For instance, the big chain stores like A&P and Piggly-Wiggly and all the big chain stores were on the White side of Jackson, and we used to have to go over there to do the family shopping, the big shopping, and we used to have to go there to the bakery... And sometimes, when you'd go through... Well, every afternoon, really, when you'd go through there, the White kids, a gang of them would be waiting on you. They would hide behind the trees in the park and wait until you'd get in the middle of them, and then jump you. So you'd have to fight your way out or out-run them, one of the two. And once you got across Capitol Street, which is the big street in Jackson, to the stores, they'd be waiting on you to come back -- so you'd have to figure out how to get back, you see... [LAUGHS HEARTILY]

Well, most of the time there was maybe two of you, and a lot of the time you would be by yourself. But usually me and my cousin, or somebody else...one of the boys in the neighborhood, we would go there. But not really go in large numbers, you know.

But yeah, they had... In the neighborhood, there would be a whole gang of them. Maybe eight or ten of them would jump one guy. So you got to out-run them or fight your way out of there. And this is what you'd have to cope with when it came to that neighborhood that you'd have to go through, you know.
